Subject: Request: Net-90 and quarterly invoicing for upcoming contract

I've attached our internal PO for reference (Acme_PO_4567.pdf). Please advise next steps and whether this requires senior approval.

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. Key points: they want Net-90 and quarterly consolidated invoices (no discount requested). Deal size estimated ~$420k ARR; SOW attached (SOW_Redwood_Acme_v3.pdf).

Question for Deal Desk / Legal: Is Net-90 allowed under our standard policy? My read: Net-30 is the default; we occasionally approve Net-60 with a manager sign-off. Net-90 seems outside policy and probably needs exec OK + finance confirmation on credit.

Can we triage:
- Credit check status (Finance)
- Any contract language changes needed for payment default and late fees (Legal/Vivek)
- Markus — would you be comfortable approving Net-90 for this strategic logistics customer if finance signs off?

Happy to set a quick call if helpful. Acme is ready to issue a PO today if we can confirm billing terms.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Fwd: Request: Net-90 and quarterly invoicing for upcoming contract

Marissa — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the SOW. I ran this through the Deal Desk checklist:

Summary:
- ARR ~ $420k; initial invoice run-rate ~$105k/quarter if quarterly invoicing is accepted.
- Customer explicitly requests Net-90 and quarterly consolidated invoices.
- No additional commercial concession requested.

Policy risk:
- Net-90 exceeds our standard approvals (Net-30 default; Net-60 requires VP Sales sign-off). Net-90 is flagged and requires exec-level approval (CRO / CFO).
- Finance will need a completed credit check and suggested requirement of ACH/Bank Transfer with Remittance Advice and no automatic early-pay discount.

Recommended path:
1) Finance (Laura) runs credit — attach result to the file.
2) Legal (Vivek) to add a clause limiting outstanding receivables (cap = 2 invoices outstanding) and a modest late fee (1.5% monthly) to mitigate risk.
3) Exec approval (Markus) to accept Net-90 with the above mitigations and no price concession.

If approved, I recommend we document Net-90 as a billing amendment on the SOW and include an invoice schedule.

Attaching: credit_check_request (I'll drop the completed report here once Laura confirms).

- Dylan
Deal Desk Analyst | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Net-90 and quarterly invoicing for upcoming contract

Marissa / Dylan — I reviewed the summary and the ARR. Acme Logistics is a strategic vertical account and the ARR justifies some flexibility, but only with risk controls in place. I approve Net-90 on the following conditions:

1) Finance (Laura) completes an on-file credit check and confirms credit limit covers at least two quarters.
2) Legal (Vivek) to add an amendment to the SOW: quarterly invoicing schedule, payment terms Net-90, late fee 1.5%/month after 90 days, and an outstanding invoices cap (no more than 2 outstanding invoices before we suspend services).
3) Payment method required: ACH or Wire (no card) and billing contacts must be provided.
4) No price or margin concessions to be granted in exchange for the extended terms.

If Finance flags elevated risk, we revert to Net-60 + security deposit equal to one quarter of invoiced amount. Once Laura confirms, we can send the amended SOW and close.

Markus Klein
Chief Revenue Officer | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Markus / Marissa — completed the credit review this morning. Summary attached (credit_report_acme_20260306.pdf).

Findings:
- Acme Logistics has a B2B payment history within acceptable bounds for the requested ARR. No outstanding liens or defaults found.
- Suggested operational controls: quarterly invoice schedule, remittance advice required on payment, and a contract clause to suspend services if >2 invoices are overdue by more than 15 days after 90-day term.

Given the assessment, Finance supports the exec approval and is comfortable with Net-90 under the controls Markus specified. We will require the SOW amendment and a signed billing addendum prior to the first invoice.
